subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs — next steps and pilot plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmehealth.com>, Laura Park <laura@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs — next steps and pilot plan

Thanks again for the time today, Sam and Laura — appreciated the candid discussion. Below is a short recap to confirm what we heard, suggested approach, and concrete next steps. Please flag anything we missed.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Token spend and unpredictable unit economics on current OpenAI / Anthropic usage.
- Rate limits and burst throttling interfering with user experience during peak windows.
- Data residency and compliance requirements tied to PHI-handling workflows.
- Occasional quality regressions (hallucinations) on safety-critical prompts.

Current stack you described
- API calls to OpenAI (completions + streaming) for chat experiences.
- Anthropic used for specific assistant-style flows and safety experiments.
- In-house prompt templates + a small L1 caching layer in front of the APIs.
- Embeddings stored in a managed vector DB (dims: 1536) used for retrieval.

Success criteria you want from a migration
- Latency parity (95th pct within 150ms of current best-effort for short prompts).
- Cost reduction target: ~40% per-token unit cost for production traffic.
- Seamless compatibility with existing OpenAI-style call patterns (streaming, stop tokens, function-like structured outputs).
- Security: VPC/private endpoints, SOC 2 evidence, KMS support for keys.
- Quality: measurable reduction in critical hallucination rate on your safety prompt set.

Model shortlist (initial candidates we discussed)
- Llama 3 family (70B quantized Q4f16) — strong latency/cost tradeoff when quantized.
- Falcon-180B-instruct (INT8) — good instruction-following, helpful as a candidate for red-team tests.
- Mistral Instruct / Mistral XXL variants — good quality-to-cost.

Proposed approach
1) Security & procurement: we’ll share SOC 2 artifacts and a short security questionnaire for your InfoSec review.
2) Compatibility check: Dev will validate tokenizer + embedding parity and confirm streaming/stop-token behavior.
3) Pilot: 4–8 week POC (dev/staging traffic) with benchmarking on latency, cost, and hallucination metrics.
4) Rollout plan: canary -> gradual traffic shift -> cutover, with fallbacks to proprietary APIs as a safety net.

Immediate next steps (requests for you)
- Can you confirm the success criteria above and share the security contact for the questionnaire (name + email)?
- Please upload the 50–100 representative prompts (and expected outputs) you want included in hallucination/regression benchmarks.
- Confirm target pilot start week (we suggested week of Nov 18).

Attachments included
- redwood-migration-checklist.xlsx (high-level pilot checklist)
- redwood-pilot-sow.pdf (sample statement of work / timelines)

If that all looks good I’ll: (a) open a HubSpot deal with the mutual action plan, (b) send a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive with Dev, and (c) share the security questionnaire.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing this.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and aligns with our notes. A few quick items: 
- Confirming the success criteria — latency, cost target (~40%), and SOC 2 evidence are must-haves for our security/compliance board.
- We will (a) share the prompt set by 11/10, (b) loop in our security contact (I’ve cc’d procurement for introduction).
- We’d like to see a short benchmark on hallucination rates vs our current OpenAI baseline before committing the pilot. Can Redwood provide a controlled comparison?

Attaching our SOW request template for your team to review: SOW_Request.pdf

Sam
Sam Jenkins
Director of AI Products | Acme Health
sam.jenkins@acmehealth.com | +1 (650) 555-3322

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs — next steps and pilot plan

Thanks for the summary, Marissa. Wanted to add a technical checklist and clarify what we’ll need to run an apples-to-apples benchmark: 
- Tokenizer / encoding parity: we’ll verify that existing prompts encode to matching token sequences or provide a mapping plan (we can run a token-diff check).
- Embedding dims: confirm your vector DB is 1536-dim; if not, we’ll map or re-embed during the pilot.
- Streaming & streaming-resume: Redwood’s runtime can support OpenAI-style chunked streaming and stop-token semantics; we’ll validate with 3 representative streaming flows.
- Deterministic seeds: to reproduce hallucination checks we’ll run multiple seeds and compute median/worst-case behaviors.
- Data path: we’ll document how PHI is handled in the pilot (ephemeral logs, encryption at-rest/in-transit, VPC endpoints).

For the controlled comparison: we’ll provision a small test harness that (1) replays your prompt set against your current OpenAI key, (2) runs against the shortlisted open models in quantized configs, and (3) produces a single PDF report with latency/cost/hallucination metrics. We can deliver that report within 7–10 business days after we receive the prompt set and security signoff.

I’ll attach a short "tech-checklist" as a one-pager in the drive link Marissa will share and block time for a deep-dive. Availability: Nov 12–14 afternoons PT for the technical kickoff.

—
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Great — thanks Sam and Dev. Quick mutual action plan and owners so we can lock calendar items: 

Mutual action plan (high level)
- By 2025-11-10: Acme to provide (a) security contact and (b) 50–100 prompt set + expected outputs (owner: Sam).
- By 2025-11-12: Redwood to share SOC 2 artifacts + security questionnaire (owner: Marissa). Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-migration
- 2025-11-12 to 2025-11-14: Technical kickoff + compatibility checks (owner: Dev). Please confirm a preferred slot and we’ll send calendar invites.
- Week of 2025-11-18: Pilot kickoff (4–8 weeks) — Redwood to provision test cluster and begin baseline benchmarking (owner: Redwood Engineering).
- By 2025-11-25: Initial benchmark report (latency / cost / hallucination metrics) delivered to Acme (owner: Dev).

Deliverables and acceptance criteria
- Acceptance: pilot must demonstrate (a) latency within agreed threshold, (b) >=40% cost improvement on token spend, and (c) no increase in critical hallucination rate vs baseline.

Next items I’ll do now
- Open the HubSpot deal and attach the mutual action plan (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345678/ACME-1357).
- Share SOC 2 artifacts and the security questionnaire (folder link above).
- Send a Doodle for Nov 12–14 for the technical kickoff.

If that timeline works I’ll send the invites and the pilot SOW draft (redwood-pilot-sow.pdf) for your review.

Best,
Marissa
